area_description:
Menschenrechte, wie sie in der Allgemeinen Erklärung der Menschenrechte und im gesamten internationalen Menschenrechtsrecht verankert sind, erkennen an, dass „alle Menschenrechte universell, unteilbar sowie voneinander abhängig und miteinander verknüpft sind“. Dazu gehören sowohl bürgerliche und politische Rechte als auch wirtschaftliche, soziale und kulturelle Rechte. Fortschritt und Menschenrechte sind untrennbar miteinander verbunden, und das eine kann kaum ohne das andere existieren. Gleichzeitig erkennen wir den Ansatz der schrittweisen Verwirklichung der Menschenrechte an, bei dem die finanziellen und sonstigen Ressourcen, die einer Regierung zur Verfügung stehen, bei der Beurteilung der Erfüllung ihrer Verpflichtungen in Bezug auf bürgerliche, soziale und wirtschaftliche Rechte berücksichtigt werden.
Quelle: "Counting What Counts: A Compass of Progress for People and Planet". Bericht der Sectretary-General`s Independent High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP (eigene Übersetzung).

en.national_indicator_available:
• Proportion of population reporting having personally felt discriminated against in their contacts with public services in the previous 12 months
  • Proportion of ever-partnered women and girls subjected to sexual violence by a current or former intimate partner in the previous 12 months
en.indicator_name:
• Proportion of population reporting having personally felt discriminated against or harassed in the previous 12 months
  • Proportion of ever-partnered women and girls subjected to physical and/or sexual violence by a current or former intimate partner in the previous 12 months
en.area_description:
Human rights, as enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the wider body of international human rights law, which recognize that “all human rights are universal, indivisible, and interdependent and interrelated”. This includes civic and political rights as well as economic, social and cultural rights. Progress and human rights are intertwined, and one can scarcely exist without the other. At the same time, we recognize the progressive realization approach to human rights, whereby consideration is given to the financial and other resources available to a government when assessing its compliance with its obligations with respect to civil, social and economic rights.
Source: "Counting What Counts: A Compass of Progress for People and Planet". Report of the Secretary-General`s Independent High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP.
en.differences:
• The data refers solely to experiences of discrimination when dealing with public services.
  • The data refers solely to sexual violence.

footer_fields.label: Notes
footer_fields.value:
• Data is only available from 2015.
  • The data refers to experiences of discrimination in the respectively preceding 24 months.
  • The data is based on a special evaluation and is not publicly available.

footer_fields.series: female victims of sexual violence by an intimate partner
footer_fields.label: Notes
footer_fields.value:
• The calculation is based on the retroactively calculated average population. This was determined for 2018 to 2021 on the basis of the 2022 census.
  • The data is based on a special evaluation and is not publicly available.
  • For victims recorded in the reporting year, the year in which the offence was committed may also be prior to the reporting year (initial statistics). Persons who were recorded as victims multiple times in the reporting year are counted multiple times accordingly.
  • Due to methodological changes, data is only available from 2018 onwards.

footer_fields.label: Notes
footer_fields.value:
• Number of victims per 100,000 inhabitants (V/100,000): Number of victims per 100,000 inhabitants, based on the population on 31 December of the previous year. Own calculation based on the 2022 census.
  • The data is based on a special evaluation and is not publicly available.
  • For victims recorded in the reporting year, the year in which the offence was committed may also be prior to the reporting year (initial statistics). Persons who were recorded as victims multiple times in the reporting year are counted multiple times accordingly.
  • Due to methodological changes, data is only available from 2018 onwards.
